recommendation: Keep this no-change audit as-is. Do not change the current Medication.code value set back to 410942007 and do not resurrect or edit Medication.package.container for this issue; any cleanup of stale unreferenced package-form value-set files should be handled as a separate terminology/build-scope cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-8061 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy correction from the DSTU1 May 2015 ballot. It reported that the MedicationFormalRepresentation link for medication codes pointed to route-of-administration value set contents; the recorded resolution said to fix the link/correct value set, but also mixed in Medication.package.container wording and the SNOMED CT is-a 410942007 medication root used by adjacent Medication.code issues.
initial_application: Historical commit 534313123abc479f1c95a22956d9992582f9743c lists 8061 and changed source/medication/valueset-medication-package-form-codes.xml from route-of-administration root 284009009 to package-form root 408102007. The adjacent Medication.code defect was applied by 6ce87fde09500c2d61c86a07ac98f49037e7d747 for FHIR-8064, changing source/medication/valueset-medication-codes.xml from 284009009 to 410942007.
additional_context: Medication is active in source/fhir.ini. Current Medication.code binds to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/medication-codes, and that value set now composes SNOMED CT is-a 763158003 medicinal product codes because later Published issue FHIR-19294 superseded the 2015 410942007 root. Current Medication no longer has Medication.package.container; package information is represented by Medication.packageSize and related current packaging guidance, while the old package-form ValueSet remains as an unreferenced historical source file with 408102007 rather than route codes. The combined branch already contains audits for FHIR-8063, FHIR-8064, FHIR-12347, and FHIR-19294. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reapplying the 2015 text would either duplicate already-audited Medication.code work, revert a later final medication-code decision, or edit a removed Medication.package.container binding surface that no longer affects the current build.
